definitions.explanation: The most basic and essential element from which everything else arises. Used to describe the underlying cause, principle, or foundation of something.

examples.japanese: {根本|こんぽん}から{見直|みなお}す{必要|ひつよう}がある。
examples.english: We need to reconsider it from the ground up.

examples.japanese: これが{問題|もんだい}の{根本|こんぽん}{的|てき}な{原因|げんいん}だ。
examples.english: This is the fundamental cause of the problem.

examples.japanese: {制度|せいど}の{根本|こんぽん}を{変|か}えなければ、{同|おな}じ{問題|もんだい}が{繰|く}り{返|かえ}される。
examples.english: If we don't change the foundation of the system, the same problems will keep recurring.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {根本|こんぽん}{的|てき}な: fundamental, radical
- {根本|こんぽん}{原因|げんいん}: root cause
- {根本|こんぽん}から{変|か}える: to change from the roots
- {根本|こんぽん}から{見直|みなお}す: to fundamentally reconsider

SIMILAR WORDS:
{根本|こんぽん} emphasizes going back to the very origin or basis. {基本|きほん} (basic, fundamental) is more neutral and practical, referring to the basics one builds on. {根底|こんてい} (foundation) is similar but often used in the phrase {根底|こんてい}にある (to underlie).
